items.body: Review by Rysiek P. — An opportunity like this certainly cannot be overlooked. Twenty years after releasing their debut album, *Armed Forces of Simantipak*, the band Khatsaturjan?whose name derives from the renowned Armenian composer Aram Khachaturian?has released a new record titled *Monolog Chronosa*. Their discography also includes two other albums - *Disconcerto Grosso* (2010) and *Beast, Machine & Man* (2015) - and their history is notable for the fact that, as early as their 2002 debut single *Aramsome Sums*, they performed their own "rock" versions of Modest Mussorgsky's *Night on Bald Mountain* and Hector Berlioz's *March to the Scaffold*. All of this was presented in progressive hard-rock arrangements that incorporated elements reminiscent of the band Gentle Giant. Furthermore, critics hailed the group's first album as a benchmark for symphonic rock. One might pessimistically remark, "But that was years ago". Yet, it is certainly worth checking out where Khatsaturjan stands today. The band's latest release comprises forty-seven minutes of music spread across seven tracks, with an album title suggesting that the passage of time is the central theme. This phenomenon is observed and described from various perspectives - including, perhaps most importantly, the human condition and the personal, often highly subjective experience of life passing by. The title of the opening track - "Lessons (On Human Obsolescence)" - gives one food for thought right from the start. However, do not expect dark, atmospheric arrangements here. The composition is remarkably balanced,almost conservative in its playing style and employs familiar progressive rock tropes, with one notable exception: a strong emphasis on vocal polyphony (a true hallmark of this album) and a more prominent role for keyboards. These two elements define the musical structure of the song, which opens with the sound of a bell before embarking on a progressive journey rich in engaging tempo shifts and instrumental virtuosity. The second track, "What Was True," takes a slightly different approach. Here, the band clearly leans toward a modern progressive sound, successfully utilizing "new textures" to craft a unique atmosphere that straddles the line between atmospheric progressive rock (or even neo-prog) and a vocal-harmony-driven ballad. Once again, vocal polyphony and synthesizers serve as the building blocks for both this specific track and the album as a whole. The track "The Dystopian Spirit Of Club Energy" also features a piano-and-synthesizer-driven sound. Yet, in this composition, the band draws upon classical music and classical time signatures. The piano sets the arrangement's course, serving as a backdrop for highly impressive vocal performances. Only halfway through does the track remind us that it is 2026, showing how a guitar-driven rhythmic boost can yield a truly successful result. Incorporating electronic elements into the arrangement only enhances the musical value of this piece, which runs over five minutes in length. It was only while listening to "Song Of Days" that I realized what truly draws me to the band's music: a delicacy and almost theatrical storytelling style, skillfully blended with classical influences, alongside magnificent tales sung with a masterful, gradual build-up of vocal intensity. With a full arsenal of musical tools at their disposal, Khatsaturjan selects only those that fit the symphonic-progressive narrative, all while keeping classical music traditions close at hand. "Song Of Days" is a perfect example of this approach. It makes brilliant use of symphonic arrangements, blending them with flawless vocal lines and weaving in thoroughly modern progressive guitar motifs to create a truly well-crafted track. "DID Memoir" shares a similar, song-oriented character. It opens with a "classic" sense of grandeur, progressive guitar work, and... such delicate vocals. Everything weaves together into a structure that challenges the listener - filled with improvisational passages that hark back to classical music and, as an added bonus, theatrical farce-style interludes appearing midway through the fourth minute. Just listen closely around the five-minute mark for a dose of rap; this element, yet another instance of the piece's stylistic multiplicity, is entirely justified given the title: "DID Memoir." While the acronym refers to Dissociative Identity Disorder, it also serves as a fitting title for the track's eclectic, multi-stylistic nature. Following a symphonic opening, the penultimate track on this magnificent album - "The Keepers of the Philosopher's Stone" - simply sends shivers down the spine with its superb vocal lines. It features backing vocals, humming passages, and a lead vocal that stands out tonally, its rough timbre lending an air of deep mystery. Yet, what makes this composition truly exceptional is the extensive and successful incorporation of motifs drawn from classical music; the violin sounds and classical time signatures transform this five-plus-minute piece into a remarkable puzzle of motifs and an intricate arrangement. A madrigal-like character, blended with thoroughly modern synthesizer and guitar sounds, seems to elevate the track's central theme - fittingly so for a song about the "Philosopher's Stone," which here truly transmutes individual notes into "gold." With this release, the end comes all too soon. Were it not for the fact that the closing track - "Mundus Meus (This World of Mine)" - employs every possible device to captivate the listener from the very first note, one might feel that the magnificent preceding track left something musically unresolved, a void that could neither be filled nor replaced. "Mundus Meus..." stands as a magnificent anthem and the perfect culmination of the album; the Latin lyrics sound both prophetic and majestic without detracting from the depth of the message. And although the track features numerous gentle prog-metal solos, it remains, at its core, a thoroughly symphonic-progressive composition. If I say that I am very - truly very - pleasantly surprised by the latest work from the group Khatsaturjan, is that recommendation enough? If not, I'll add that the band features essentially the same lineup as on their debut and subsequent albums, even though musical light-years have passed since that first release (in 2002). Atte Kurri (vocals, bass, keyboards), Ilkka Piispala (vocals, drums, keyboards, bass), and Ilkka Saarikivi (vocals, keyboards, bass, violin) continue to demonstrate that musical trends don't matter to them. It is significant that Khatsaturjan is a group of friends who get together only when they want to record something; they are not a band that makes a living from touring and recording albums. On their Facebook page, the band writes: "We work slowly because Khatsaturjan is not our profession - it is a passion project and a beloved hobby. Whenever we decide to work on a new album, we know a years-long effort lies ahead, with no financial reward whatsoever. Yet, time and again, we take on new projects." Perhaps this approach allows them to maintain a sense of detachment and find the tranquility needed to create new music? You surely know that things tend to flow more easily when there are no deadlines hanging over your head. And since we will likely have to wait a long time for the next sign of musical life from Khatsaturjan, we should simply enjoy this highly successful release - one that has earned a spot in my top ten albums of the year.

items.body: Manufracture Music release the single “System Apathy” on 20 October 2026, under a pre-order campaign already live on Bandcamp. The Vienna-based project, run by producer Valerian Steel, built the track entirely on analog synthesizers, drum machines and raw voltage, with no software instruments involved. System Apathy by Manufracture Music The Bandcamp description describes the release as continuing the project’s A.C.I. concept, short for Analog Core Industrial: “Manufracture Music operates on a strict hardware-first philosophy. […] Forged in Vienna, ‘System Apathy’ is built entirely on unforgiving analog synthesizers, drum machines, and raw voltage. The physical behavior of the machines – their limitations, imperfections, and textures – becomes the composition itself.” Steel described the approach directly to Side-Line as “a cold, relentless EBM transmission born from technological friction and dystopian sound design.” Manufracture Music’s second A.C.I. release “System Apathy” follows “The Scene Lies (A.C.I. Manifesto)“, the two-track statement Manufracture Music released on 14 August 2026 that introduced A.C.I. as a stated concept: hardware-only production positioned against generative AI tools in the electronic underground. Where that release took the form of a spoken-word manifesto, “System Apathy” returns the project to song form while keeping the same zero-software constraint. About Manufracture Music Manufracture Music is the industrial, EBM and darkwave project of producer Valerian Steel, based in Vienna, Austria. He also runs the dance-oriented Fourtyfication*5 and the ambient-leaning Music of Synergia under his own name, and has worked with a vocalist credited only as Enzo across several Manufracture Music tracks. The debut album “Fractured Empires” appeared in early 2025, followed by the “Mormon” EP on 29 March 2025 and a run of singles through 2025 and 2026, including “Isolated”, “Ghosts” featuring Enzo, “Blood Syntax”, “Hateration”, “Tearfall”, “End of Life”, “Null Rite System” featuring Enzo, “Kinetic Decay”, “Skip My Tracks” and “Synthetic Species”. “The Scene Lies (A.C.I. Manifesto)” introduced the A.C.I. concept on 14 August 2026, and “System Apathy” now becomes the second release built under that same hardware-only method, due 20 October 2026.
items._cn_summary: 本文介绍Manufracture Music的单曲《System Apathy》，由维也纳制作人Valerian Steel主导，全程使用模拟合成器、鼓机和原始电压信号完成制作，无任何软件乐器介入。该曲目延续了项目提出的A.C.I.（Analog Core Industrial）概念，即坚持硬件优先的制作哲学，明确与生成式AI工具划清界限。前作《The Scene Lies》以朗诵式宣言形式阐述理念，而《System Apathy》则回归歌曲形式，将硬件设备的局限性、不完美与质感作为创作核心。制作人将其描述为冰冷、持续推进的EBM输出，融合技术摩擦感与反乌托邦声音设计。项目此前已发行专辑《Fractured Empires》及多支单曲，风格横跨工业、EBM与暗潮，体现出对模拟硬件美学的系统化探索。

Ivo Watts-Russell and producer John Fryer recorded and mixed “Filigr
items.body: This Mortal Coil, the rotating collective of musicians and vocalists assembled by 4AD founder Ivo Watts-Russell, released its second studio album, “Filigree & Shadow,” on 22 September 1986 through 4AD. The double LP turns 40 this year. The album gathered 25 tracks, about half of them instrumental, credited to This Mortal Coil but built around a different set of contributors than the project’s 1984 debut. Ivo Watts-Russell and producer John Fryer recorded and mixed “Filigree & Shadow” at Blackwing and Palladium Studios, with arrangements from Simon Raymonde of Cocteau Twins, cellist Martin McCarrick and engineer John Turner, plus violin and viola from Gini Ball. Dead Can Dance percussionist Peter Ulrich and members of Dif Juz, The Wolfgang Press and Colourbox also appeared on the record. Vocalists including Dominic Appleton of Breathless and Alison Limerick sang cover interpretations of songs by Tim Buckley, Gene Clark, Van Morrison, Colin Newman and Talking Heads. “Filigree & Shadow” reached number 53 on the UK Albums Chart and number 2 on the UK Indie Chart, and it streams on Spotify. About This Mortal Coil Ivo Watts-Russell founded 4AD in London in 1980 and built This Mortal Coil a few years later to record music outside the constraints of a fixed band. In 1983 he brought together Cocteau Twins’ Elizabeth Fraser and Robin Guthrie, Cindytalk’s Gordon Sharp and members of Modern English to re-record two Modern English songs as the medley “Sixteen Days/Gathering Dust.” Its B-side, a cover of Tim Buckley’s “Song to the Siren” sung by Fraser and Guthrie alone, entered the UK Singles Chart at number 66 and led Watts-Russell to build a full album around the same idea. That album, “It’ll End in Tears,” followed in 1984 on 4AD. This Mortal Coil never had a fixed lineup. Watts-Russell and engineer John Fryer were its only constant members, and each record drew on a different group of musicians and singers, most pulled from 4AD’s own roster. “Filigree & Shadow” followed in 1986 as the project’s second album, again produced by Watts-Russell and Fryer, with Simon Raymonde, Martin McCarrick and Gini Ball forming its core backing group and Peter Ulrich among the guest musicians. This Mortal Coil closed its studio run with “Blood” in 1991, on which vocalist Caroline Crawley – whose death Side-Line reported in 2016 – was among the featured singers. After the group’s run ended, Watts-Russell continued the same collaborative approach under the name The Hope Blister from 1998, while Fryer went on to produce and engineer widely across the 4AD roster and beyond. “Filigree & Shadow” turns 40 this year, four decades into a project that treated an album as a collaboration rather than the work of a fixed band.
items._genre: post-punk / darkwave / dream pop / experimental / ambient
items._cn_summary: This Mortal Coil 是 4AD 厂牌创始人 Ivo Watts-Russell 策划的流动集体项目，《Filigree & Shadow》是其 1986 年发行的第二张全长专辑，收录 25 首曲目约半数为器乐作品。项目打破了固定乐队的常规模式，每张专辑召集不同的音乐人和歌手参与录制，本次核心班底包括 Cocteau Twins 的 Simon Raymonde、大提琴手 Martin McCarrick 与小提琴手 Gini Ball，Dead Can Dance 的 Peter Ulrich 等亦贡献了打击乐。人声部分由 Breathless 的 Dominic Appleton、Alison Limerick 等演绎 Tim Buckley、Van Morrison、Gene Clark、Colin Newman 与 Talking Heads 等人的翻唱作品。制作层面由 Watts-Russell 与 John Fryer 在 Blackwing 和 Palladium Studios 完成录音混音，编曲注重弦乐铺陈与氛围营造。该项目将专辑视为一次集体协作而非固定乐队的成果，延续了 4AD 厂牌标志性的阴郁美学与跨流派实验精神。

items.body: Pray for me tonight Blinded by your light Stigmatize my mind Your lost paradise Anton, a Parisian post-punk project led by Anton Steinbock, carries itself with the severe romanticism of someone who owns more black coats than practical shoes, but their recent single Répression finds that severity loosening into something stranger, more fevered, and considerably more dangerous. Working with fellow coldwave artist Tout Debord, Steinbock pushes his music toward a place where devotion and psychic collapse keep borrowing each other’s clothes, while Leonid Diaghilev’s production gives the track enough space to breathe without sanding away its cold edge. The guitars ring out in pale, eerie streaks, recalling Clan of Xymox during their 4AD era, while the bass keeps the floor beneath everything firm and deliberate. Synths reminiscent of Asylum Party and Little Nemo deepen the song’s French coldwave character, and its brooding melancholy brings to mind Scottish band Lowlife. Anton keeps these affinities personal through Steinbock’s low, echoing delivery and the movement between French and English. His voice sounds less like a performance than a private argument accidentally amplified through the walls of an empty Church. This tension suits the lyrics, which circle despair, fixation, religious need, and the exhausting effort of trying to escape thoughts that have already memorized the route home. Emptiness becomes almost physical here, while religious language turns love into a strange transaction involving devotion, punishment, salvation, and sacrifice. There is a plea buried inside the song, though Anton wisely lets it remain uneasy. Comfort carries a price, paradise looks compromised, and the promise of another night together begins to resemble a trap with excellent lighting. Tout Debord’s video takes those concerns and gives them a suitably Catholic mindspace. Performance footage is layered over religious images, cemeteries, stone, and monuments, with additional cinematography by Sylvester Engbrox adding another layer of distance between the body and whatever eternity is supposed to mean. The images of permanence become almost sarcastic beside a song obsessed with emotional states that keep mutating by the hour. Faith may promise forever; the people on screen still have to get through tonight. Watch the video for Répression below: Répression also marks a useful turn after Never Freed Myself, continuing Anton’s taste for austere post-punk while sharpening the drama and widening the frame. Since the project began in 2024, Steinbock has moved quickly from solo recordings to a live configuration with Gabriela Guyez, building a set that can pivot from harder post-punk material toward synth-heavy darkwave ballads. Répression works best as a collision between movement and paralysis: the body gets the beat, the mind gets the bad news, and the track keeps one boot planted firmly on the dance floor. Anton has made a song for anyone who has ever mistaken obsession for revelation and then had to live through the morning after. Listen to Répression below and order the single here. Répression by Anton, Tout Debord Follow Anton: Bandcamp Spotify Facebook Instagram YouTube The post “Pray For Me Tonight” — Anton and Tout Debord Share Video for French Coldwave Confessional “Répression” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 巴黎后朋克项目Anton与冷潮艺术家Tout Debord合作的单曲《Répression》，在严峻浪漫主义基调上融入了更迷乱、更具危险感的元素。制作人Leonid Diaghilev保留了冷峻边缘的同时给予呼吸空间，吉他音色苍白诡异，呼应Clan of Xymox的4AD时期，贝斯沉稳，合成器借鉴Asylum Party与Little Nemo，整体弥漫苏格兰乐队Lowlife式的阴郁忧郁。Steinbock低回回声式的人声表演，介于私密争吵与教堂回响之间，歌词围绕绝望、执念、宗教渴求与逃离无望的思绪展开，将爱转化为涉及奉献、惩罚、救赎与牺牲的奇异交易。音乐录影带叠加宗教影像、墓地与纪念碑，以天主教意象呼应歌曲主题。作为继《Never Freed Myself》之后的发展，作品在运动与麻痹之间形成碰撞，身体获得节拍，心灵承受坏消息。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，五首曲目围绕传统北欧民谣展开。Guldhammer作为北欧民谣圈内经验丰富的声乐核心，嗓音浑厚而有说服力，作品散发古老而粗粝的氛围。配器上融合口琴、风笛、铙钹、长笛与弦乐，传统旋律在粗粝节奏与非常规律动下被重新塑形，如'Orms'一曲将口琴与弦乐、长笛交织，制造出令人不安又不失灵动的器乐织体。乐评指出乐队虽为新人却已展现出成熟的艺术判断力，对传统材料的处理并非简单复刻，而是带有实验性的个人解读，为后续全长专辑留下了值得期待的创作空间。

Comprised of four long-form tracks, the project came about from conversations that the two artists, on opposite sides of the world, had in 2021 about the volatile environments that they found themselves in, as Australia experience flooding and extreme weather, and Ireland's Atlantic coastline was hit by storms. items.body: Review by kenethlevine — Knowing that DANDO SHAFT was to add POLLY BOLTON as full time member for their eponymous 2nd album, I would have predicted such an infusion to be just what the doctor ordered for balance and groundedness. Paradoxically, this is a notably superior effort yet the 2 tracks on which she sings are among the weaker entries, not bad at all like the inane "Pass it on" but not nearly the equals of the authentic charms of the TIR NA NOG like ballad "Sometimes"; the lively spiritual endeavor of "Waves upon the ether", the sheer charm of "Whispering Ned", and the jaw dropping prog folk exuberance of "Kalyope Driver", their best by far to this point. The Anglo-Celtic flourishes are better integrated than on the debut even if they insist on weightlessly superficial 30 second interludes. A bonus cut on "An Evening with Dando Shaft" does suggest better things ahead with Ms. Bolton and indeed she may well have helped more than mere credits and front line contributions might imply. As you are discovering this unjustly suppressed talented collective along with me, I can only add that time will tell as we pivot freely through history from our advantage point.

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — In the early 2000s, Savatage's core members were juggling their time and musical ideas between the band and the increasingly demanding side project Trans-Siberian Orchestra, created by Jon Oliva, producer Paul O'Neill, and arranger and keyboardist Robert Kinkel. It was against this hectic backdrop that the American band released "Poets and Madmen" (2001), their eleventh album, whose central theme revolves around a loose adaptation inspired by the tragic fate of Kevin Carter, the photographer who captured the harrowing image of a Sudanese child crouching on the ground, watched from a short distance by a vultur - a photograph that earned him the Pulitzer Prize in 1994.The album features the return of Oliva's raw and expressive voice as lead singer, a greater prominence of Chris Caffery's rhythmic and heavy guitar riffs, and a solid instrumental foundation, supported by Kinkel's symphonic arrangements. All of this lends, on the one hand, that combination of theatrical stage presence and razor-sharp energy characteristic of metal outbursts in tracks like the anguished "Stay with Me a While", the martial "Commissar," and, above all, the epic "Morphine Child", an elaborate and highly fluid epic that includes superb choral segments and is surely the jewel of the album.On the other hand, there's room to revisit the genre's raw, primal roots with the fast-paced, '80s-style heavy track "Drive"; the density of doom metal with Sabbath-esque touches in "I Seek Power" - another great track - ; and the pasty "Awaken," with Oliva on the verge of vocal breakdown. There are also some acoustic subtleties in hybrid tracks like "The Rumour (Jesus)" and "Man on the Mirror", where the band navigates peaceful valleys and abrupt instrumental mood shifts with great skill.The self-indulgent and theatrical "Got to Get Back to a Reason" - a track that attempts to capture the emotion in the air and give the album an epic, redemptive ending - ends up also being the final piece in the band's discography. Because, despite the musicians' intention to maintain both projects simultaneously, their packed schedules and commitments made their coexistence unsustainable. After the album's promotional tour and in the absence of an official statement, Savatage went on a "hiatus" that has now lasted 25 years...3.5/4 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / heavy metal / symphonic metal / doom metal
items._cn_summary: Savatage 2001年第十一张专辑以南非摄影师凯文·卡特拍摄秃鹫与饥饿苏丹儿童的悲剧命运为核心概念展开。Jon Oliva 回归主唱位置，其粗犷而富有表现力的嗓音与 Chris Caffery 的厚重吉他律动交织成戏剧化张力。专辑在两条线索之间游走：一方面呈现《Stay with Me a While》《Morphine Child》等极具剧场感的金属篇章，其中后者以复杂结构和合唱段落成为亮点；另一方面回归根源金属速度感（《Drive》）、Doom 密度（《I Seek Power》），并在《The Rumour》《Man on the Mirror》中以原声段落制造情绪转折。Kinkel 的交响编曲为整体提供了宏大底色。由于乐队成员同时投入 Trans-Siberian Orchestra 项目，本专辑也意外成为乐队的最终作品，随后进入长达二十五年的休整期。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — The surname Gildenl'w is by no means unfamiliar to us. There's no need to explain why here. But it might be worth dwelling a bit on his first name. Born in Sweden, Kristoffer was the bassist for Pain of Salvation up until the double album *Be* (2004), and like most bassists, his demeanor was more low-key at the time, and his role seemingly less prominent than that of his brother, the frontman. Can we then speak of emancipation? Or simply of a search for another form of personal fulfillment? In any case, in 2003, at the height of the famous progressive metal band's popularity, Kristoffer left Sweden and Pain of Salvation to move to the Netherlands, collaborating on both sides of the Atlantic with some heavyweights of the progressive rock scene (Damien Wilson, Neal Morse, Lana Lane, the band Kayak'), before launching a solo career in 2012 with the album *Rust*.Begun in 2019 (alongside the album *Homebound*), *Empty*, Kristoffer Gildenl'w's fifth and latest solo album, was originally scheduled for 2020, but a devastating pandemic had other plans, and an unexpected *Let Me Be A Ghost* took precedence, releasing in 2021. Despite its overarching theme (depression), the album *Let Me Be A Ghost* still contained beautiful moments of musical serenity, a touch of melodic and harmonic lightness, as if weightless. There was gravity, too, but it knew how to be playful at times. And this ghostly imprint ultimately led to a kind of peace. 'Let Me Be A Ghost' seemed to describe the sensation of falling'but a fall from which one gets back up, with difficulty, not without effort, yet with courage and the feeling of having grown.'Empty' is even more striking because it offers a broader critical perspective on another tragic fall'that of humanity, drawn into the emptiness of our existence. The music thus becomes the anxious echo of a palpable despair that conveys the state of mind of a man struggling not to fall into this void'this vast, searing void that weighs on our hearts, terrified at the thought of what humanity is doing, a lost humanity in search of meaning.Like his previous solo albums, *Empty* possesses the same strange power of attraction'an irresistible pull that draws us entirely into a universe poised between dream and reality, between soothing light and revealing darkness. How can one resist lyrics so beautiful, so poignant'all these words that soar directly toward the heavens, sung in that deep, comforting, instantly recognizable voice that speaks of disarray, doubt, the pain of incomprehension in the face of human beings' self-destructive recklessness'a voice that speaks to us of our fears and sufferings as fragile beings, just as one might speak to a damned soul waiting in vain for its due.Despite all, one senses the presence of a mystery'a reflection on our purpose in life'carried by Kristoffer Gildenl'w's music and the brilliant artists who perform it. Each composition is a bewildering showcase of beauty, set to restrained vocals, but that is precisely what makes Kristoffer's style so powerful and heightens the emotional vertigo it evokes in us. Each track on his album is a profound and expansive anthem that can help us endure all the torments of the world. We can sense echoes of his former band. We can sense his love for Joni Mitchell, Mike Oldfield, and other giants of the '70s. We hear echoes of Anathema or Dire Straits. We encounter heart-wrenching blues ' la Pink Floyd, the kind whose mysteries were known only to Gilmour and Waters when they were still able to get along. It is dark and dense music, yet it regularly lightens, expands, shakes itself free, moves, and brightens'notably thanks to the graceful arabesques of Ben Mathot and Anne Bakker's violins, a rhythm section capable of softening its touch, the enchanting piano arpeggios played by Kristoffer himself, or the memorable feverish surges of the electric guitar tamed by sorcerers who seem to command the waves and the flames; all these warm notes like so many stars burning eternally to soothe our nights.*Empty* is one of those rich and profound progressive rock works that give us all the more the more we bring of ourselves to them as we receive them'intuitively felt by the heart yet always surprising to the ear. By giving us the best of himself here'which requires great courage' Kristoffer Gildenl'w sets an example by casting an intense light into the night of our troubled souls, illuminating with irrepressible hope a reality before which the malevolent structures of our destructive imagination and our death-dealing impulses dissolve'the only true light, the one that seeks to purify us of our unforgivable sins committed against Mother Nature. In the end, 'Empty' is neither sad nor despairing. In any case, even in the face of impending disaster, there will always be something good to take away'if only a tiny drop of happiness or a pinch of love.
items._genre: crossover prog / progressive rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Kristoffer Gildenlöw第五张个人专辑，他曾任Pain of Salvation贝斯手，后移居荷兰与多位前卫摇滚音乐人合作。专辑原定2020年发行，因疫情延后，期间穿插了2021年的《Let Me Be A Ghost》。作品延续了其个人系列的一贯特质——在梦境与现实、安抚之光与揭示之暗之间游走。评论重点强调了人声的辨识度与歌词的诗意性，认为词作直击人类自我毁灭的困境。音乐呈现出对人类堕入存在空虚的批判视角，以焦虑的回响承载绝望情绪，同时暗含对生命目的的反思。评论文章在描述作品情感氛围与主题意涵方面较为充分。

items.body: Devoted BJ released the single “Ich kann nicht schlafen” on September 11, 2026, through KL Dark Records. Devoted BJ brings a sound that mixes dark pop and pop dance with 80s-style electro synths and industrial percussion. “Ich kann nicht schlafen” is Devoted BJ’s second single of 2026, following “Schatten in der Nacht”, which the same label issued on June 26, 2026. The new track marks a further step in his development as a songwriter alongside the same synth-driven sound, and a further single is already in the works. Beyond Spotify, the single is also available for download through Apple Music, Beatport and Amazon. KL Dark Records and ‘Ich kann nicht schlafen’ KL Dark Records operates as both an artist agency and a label, working across synth pop, dark pop, dark electro, EBM, body pop, gothic, dark wave and industrial. About Devoted BJ Devoted BJ released the “Space Time Energy RMX” EP five years before “Ich kann nicht schlafen.” His return to new material began in 2026 with “Schatten in der Nacht,” issued through KL Dark Records on June 26, and continued on September 11 with “Ich kann nicht schlafen,” released through the same label. A further single is already planned. No other biographical detail beyond the label’s own material could be independently verified at the time of writing.

items.body: Zwickau’s Elektrisch Festival returns on 24 October 2026 with a line-up that makes a convincing argument for electronic music as a continuum rather than a museum of separate generations. At one end stands Portion Control, active since 1979 and fundamental to the development of British industrial electronics; around them are Hungarian EBM veterans Escalator, the much newer KRIEG-B, and the contemporary projects OSZYLAYTER and Cyborg Projekt X. The 19th Elektrisch Festival takes place at Club Seilerstraße, Seilerstraße 1B, 08056 Zwickau. Doors open at 19:00, with the programme beginning at 20:00. The final line-up announced by organiser emmobiz Records is Portion Control, Escalator, OSZYLAYTER, Cyborg Projekt X and KRIEG-B. A festival with a rather unusual history Elektrisch is not a newly invented festival carrying an impressive number. Its history reaches back well before the current revival. Contemporary reports document the 11th edition in 2007, the 12th in 2008, the 13th in 2009, and two editions, numbers 14 and 15, in 2010, then held at Zwickau’s BPM Club. Artists appearing during that period included names such as Absolute Body Control, Birmingham 6, Tyske Ludder and The Klinik. Then Elektrisch disappeared for fourteen years. emmobiz Records revived it in 2024 with the 16th Elektrisch Festival, now at Club Seilerstraße. That return was already sold out months in advance and brought together Calva Y Nada, Cat Rapes Dog, Digital Factor and Accessory. The 17th edition followed in October 2025 with Test Dept, NZ, In Strict Confidence, Supreme Court and To Avoid. In February 2026, the 18th Elektrisch expanded across two evenings, separating a synthpop-oriented first night from a harder EBM/electro programme on the second. That history makes the 2026 autumn line-up apt: Elektrisch has repeatedly connected artists from different phases of underground electronic music instead of reducing EBM to one historical period. Portion Control The obvious historical heavyweight is Portion Control. Formed in London in 1979, the group emerged from the early British industrial-electronic underground and became important for its use of synthesisers, drum machines and sampling long before those methods became standard practice. Their influence has subsequently been acknowledged in connection with artists including Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, Nine Inch Nails, Orbital and Nitzer Ebb; they also toured with Depeche Mode in 1984. But calling Portion Control a heritage act would miss what remains interesting about them. They returned in the 2000s and have continued producing new work rather than maintaining the early catalogue. This August they released “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…”, their first major Artoffact archival box, while their official site simultaneously continues to define the project rather succinctly as “uncompromising dark electronic audio.” Zwickau is currently one of only two forthcoming live appearances listed on their Bandcamp. Escalator Escalator brings another kind of history to the evening. The Hungarian project was founded in Budapest in 1988 by 2RT+TB and belongs to the late-’80s/early-’90s generation of European Electronic Body Music. Its musical roots lie in the harder intersection of EBM and industrial electronics, with early influences including Kraftwerk, Throbbing Gristle, Cabaret Voltaire, Clock DVA and Front 242. Escalator’s history has been anything but linear; long gaps between releases and activity have been part of the project, yet its work has remained closely associated with the physical, stripped-back mechanics of classic body music. Their presence next to Portion Control is more than an “old-school” pairing: the two acts come from different geographical and chronological points in the development of electronic body music. OSZYLAYTER The German OSZYLAYTER represents a much more recent strand of the line-up. Public biographical information on the project is relatively sparse, so it is better not to manufacture a grand history that isn’t there. What can be verified is a growing Bandcamp catalogue including “Hate This Day”, “Lover Boy”, “Free Girls” and “Dig It in the Dirt”, while current Elektrisch coverage places the project on the modern dark-electro/industrial side of the bill. In the context of Elektrisch, that relative newness is actually useful. This isn’t five bands demonstrating variations of exactly the same established EBM formula; OSZYLAYTER helps shift the evening toward newer club electronics and shows where some of those older physical principles have travelled. Cyborg Projekt X Cyborg Projekt X is similarly one of the less extensively documented names on the programme. The confirmed festival announcement places the project alongside OSZYLAYTER as part of the contemporary dark-electro and industrial side of the line-up, with an emphasis on forceful, club-oriented electronics. That makes Cyborg Projekt X something of the unknown variable of the evening, especially for listeners arriving primarily for the established EBM names. In a festival whose history has always mixed recognised acts with smaller projects, that is hardly out of character. KRIEG-B KRIEG-B is much newer as a project but comes with considerable history behind its members. The duo was formed in June 2023 by Dominique Lallement, known from Kriegbereit, Cobalt 60 and K-Bereit, and Benoît Buyse, associated with Dreadfool, Anamorphosis and Nihiliste. The project describes its music as a meeting point between industrial electronics, EBM and darkwave, drawing on several decades of electronic music rather than one specific period. Their debut album “War Drums’ Resonance” arrived in November 2024, with tracks including “S.C.S.N”, “Parabellum”, “Artificial Minds”, “Truth Lies” and “King of Emptiness”. In a sense, KRIEG-B makes a neat closing piece to the Elektrisch concept: a young project constructed by musicians carrying several earlier generations of European industrial electronics with them. More than the line-up The revived Elektrisch has also developed a strong physical-release component. The 18th edition was accompanied by exclusive 10-inch festival vinyl releases, while emmobiz has already announced a V.A. “19. Elektrisch Festival” 10-inch connected to this year’s event. The appeal of the 19th edition goes beyond Portion Control finally returning to Zwickau. The five acts represent very different positions within the same broad history: British industrial experimentation, Hungarian old-school EBM, contemporary German dark electronics, and a new Franco-Belgian project carrying the experience of earlier industrial formations into something current. That is probably the strongest reason to pay attention to Elektrisch. After a fourteen-year absence, the festival did not return simply to recreate the period in which it originally existed. Its current identity depends on putting that history into the same room with what came after it. 19. Elektrisch Festival: date, venue and line-up Elektrisch Festival 24 October 2026 Club Seilerstraße Seilerstraße 1B, 08056 Zwickau, Germany Line-up: Portion Control Escalator OSZYLAYTER Cyborg Projekt X KRIEG-B Doors: 19:00 Start: 20:00 Tickets are available through emmobiz Records.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义的乐评，而是关于德国茨维考市第19届Elektrisch音乐节的演出预告与历史梳理。文章重点介绍了2026年秋季音乐节的阵容，包括自1979年活跃至今的英国工业电子先驱Portion Control、匈牙利EBM老将Escalator，以及KRIEG-B、OSZYLAYTER和Cyborg Projekt X等较新项目。文章追溯了音乐节的历史脉络，从2007年的第11届到2010年的第15届在BPM Club举办，期间沉寂十四年，后由emmobiz Records厂牌于2024年重启并移至Club Seilerstraße。文章详述了Portion Control在早期英国工业电子场景中的地位及其对后续艺术家如Skinny Puppy、Nine Inch Nails的影响，强调该音乐节持续连接不同世代的地下电子音乐人，而非将EBM局限于某一历史阶段。整体内容偏新闻性质，缺乏对音乐本身的深度分析。

items.body: Ms Xxan released the nine-track album “Make Yourself the Lie” on September 8, 2026, via VuMantra Records, available as a free, name-your-price download on Bandcamp. Ms Xxan performs the album’s spoken word poetry herself, processing her voice through synthesized effects and building the backing from dark ambient and noise-industrial soundscapes, with every credit on the record, from writing through final mix, going to her alone. The album carries a content warning for strong and explicit lyrics; depression under present-day conditions runs through its themes, and the nine tracks grow steadily heavier as the sequence progresses: “make yourself the lie.”, “psychic break.”, “doctrine of harm.”, “dissociative parallels.”, “crossing over.”, “discontinuance.”, “disremember.”, “anhedonia.” and “hatchling.” The same material is also published in episode form as the “Ms Xxan” podcast, available on Apple Podcasts and Audiomack, and streams on SoundCloud alongside the Bandcamp release. Make Yourself the Lie by Ms Xxan About Ms Xxan Ms Xxan writes and produces spoken word and industrial noise music from her current base in the Pacific Northwest, a home she plans to leave before long. “Make Yourself the Lie”, released September 8, 2026, is her album for VuMantra Records, a Berlin-based label founded by Vū (Vince Gagliardi) in 2019, who also records as The Nent and LAGÁN. VuMantra describes its output as “endarkening rhythms for dystopic sub-cultures”, with a catalog built on percussive, ritualistic and tribalistic electronic music. “Make Yourself the Lie” was written, performed, composed, produced and mixed entirely by Ms Xxan, and stands as her first release documented on the label alongside the parallel “Ms Xxan” podcast series carrying the same material.

items.body: German medieval techno act Klangschmiede & Friends released the single “Remember” on September 1, 2026, and submitted it as an application for Germany’s national selection process for the Eurovision Song Contest 2027. The full application was uploaded to public broadcaster SWR on the same day; German participation in the 2027 contest is not yet confirmed. Live bagpipes, hurdy-gurdy and flute sit alongside electronic production on “Remember,” with English lyrics and passages in Old High German drawn from early medieval sources such as the Hildebrandslied. The track runs just under three minutes and moves between medieval techno, dark electronic production and historical folk balladry. Klangschmiede & Friends’ Eurovision 2027 bid For the submission, Klangschmiede expanded into the extended line-up Klangschmiede & Friends, bringing in additional musicians for the song’s acoustic instrumentation. The official music video was filmed with the full ensemble at Schloss Burg in Solingen on August 17, 2026. Regional public broadcaster WDR was on site for the shoot and aired a television feature on the production through its Lokalzeit Bergisches Land program. The submission has also drawn coverage from ESC kompakt and regional newspapers including the Solinger Tageblatt and the Remscheider General-Anzeiger. About Klangschmiede Klangschmiede is the duo of Claudia Sokoll and Timo Tofaute, based in the Bergisches Land region of Germany and operating officially since 2025. The project mixes medieval and Nordic folk elements with electronic production, drawing on historical sources such as the Hildebrandslied, the Poetic Edda and Nordic ballads. Its catalog includes the album “RITUS”, released digitally and on CD on May 14, 2026, and singles including “Nothing We Love Is Ever Gone” (March 26, 2026), “Hüter der Straße” (April 30, 2026) and “Solringen” (July 23, 2026), alongside a remix of “Tanz den Feuertanz” featuring Keltania. Klangschmiede has also worked with the medieval folk-rock band Corvus Corax on the track “Ragnarök”. “Remember”, released as a single on September 1, 2026 under the expanded name Klangschmiede & Friends, is the project’s submission for Germany’s national Eurovision Song Contest 2027 selection, with participation still to be confirmed.

items._cn_summary: 德国双人组Klangschmiede与扩展阵容合作的单曲《Remember》以中世纪乐器（风笛、手摇风琴、长笛）与电子制作相结合，歌词混合英语与古高地德语，取材自《希尔德布兰特之歌》等早期中世纪文献。作品在Medieval Techno、暗电子与历史民谣叙事之间切换，时长不到三分钟。该曲已提交德国2027年欧洲歌唱大赛国家遴选流程，官方MV在索林根的Burg城堡取景拍摄。乐队此前已发行专辑《RITUS》及多首单曲，并与中世纪民谣摇滚乐队Corvus Corax有过合作。文章本质为新闻通讯稿，缺乏对音乐本身的深度乐评分析，仅提供事件与曲目背景信息。作为融合中世纪民谣与电子节拍的小众跨界作品，与实验电子及世界音乐口味存在一定契合，但内容为纯新闻报道而非原创评论。

items.body: Italian musician Ystrith released the seven-track dark ambient debut album “The M Rites” on 2 September 2026, self-issued on Bandcamp and also available on Spotify. Across its seven tracks, Ystrith works with Mithraic mystery-cult imagery, the Roman-era worship of the god Mithras, pulling on details like its buried temples and the weathered carvings its followers left behind. The M Rites by Ystrith Ystrith described the album to Side-Line as concerned not only with the surviving relics of the Mithraic cult, but with “the unbridgeable distance between the surviving objects of the cult and the experiences that have been lost with time.” The seven tracks – “Cautes”, “Fading Gates (of Cosmic Enlightenment)”, “Marble Tauroctonies”, “Myth of the Petrogenesis”, “Voces Magicae”, “Solstice at the Spelaeum” and “Cautopates” – take their titles directly from Mithraic iconography and ritual: Cautes and Cautopates are the torch-bearing twin attendants of Mithras in Roman relief carvings, while “tauroctonies” refers to the bull-slaying scene at the centre of Mithraic imagery. Ystrith has described the record’s musical language as moving through “slow metamorphoses, obsessive repetition and dark, suspended atmospheres,” sustained across the album’s running time to match its ritual subject matter. About Ystrith Ystrith is an Italian musician who records ambient and dark ambient music. “The M Rites”, released 2 September 2026, is the project’s debut album, presented as a sustained meditation on the Mithraic mysteries rather than a single-themed track or EP. The release is available to stream on Bandcamp and Spotify.
items._cn_summary: 意大利音乐人Ystrith首张专辑《The M Rites》以罗马密特拉教崇拜为概念核心，引用其地下神庙、浮雕雕刻与牛祭图景等物质遗迹，构建一段关于仪式主题的持续冥想。七首作品标题直接取自密特拉教图像体系，如持火炬的双侍从、神秘入口、魔法之声、冬至洞穴仪式等，文本与音乐结构紧密咬合。作曲手法强调缓慢演变、执着重复与幽暗悬浮的氛围，与宗教仪式的冥想性形成统一调性。发行方式为独立自发行，仅在Bandcamp与Spotify上架。作为暗潮/氛围音乐范畴内的类型化作品，概念建构扎实但未能从文中展现出突破常规的声响创新或跨类型融合。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 专辑以1819年曼彻斯特彼得广场屠杀事件为背景，Sean Cooney创作原创歌曲重访这段英国工人阶级历史。专辑以图书形式呈现，收录同时代信件、政治漫画与插图，形成多媒体体验。编曲采用小型室内编制，吉他手Sam Carter、小提琴手兼歌手Eliza Carthy、贝斯手Ben Nicholls以及兰开夏工业民谣歌手Jennifer Reid共同参与。歌曲捕捉集会当日的氛围——从期待与兴奋，到军队冲入后变为恐惧与奔逃，再到悲痛的余波。Cooney以个人化视角聚焦Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等小人物故事，同时以三段短曲刻画士兵的傲慢。这张专辑在当下全球政府打压抗议的背景下，提供了一段历史教训的回顾。整体属于英伦叙事民谣传统，未涉及实验或前卫元素。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — In 1971, Biblical themes and rock operas were all the rage. This was David's contribution to the phenomenon. Though recorded in LA with a 38-piece orchestra (including bassist Carol Kaye, keyboard specialist Don Randi, and guitarist Mike Deasy), the lead vocalists are only listed as the singing group "The Dillons" while David's friend Julian "Cannonball" Adderley politely serves as the album's producer.A1. "Overture" (5:49) the first half is bombastic symphony orchestra, very well composed and rendered--like an overture. At the 2:45 mark there is a stoppage which is slowly filled by wah-wah-electric guitar, electric bass, funk-rock drumming, and dirty/raunchy electric piano as the orchestra horns and strings re-engage, only in more of a support/accent role--though their melodic presentation is continuous of those melodies presented in the opening half. Very cool! Very solid and well-rendered and powerful. (9.5/10)A2. "Comfort Ye My People" (2:45) Elton John-like solo piano opens this before male tenor voice enters to sing the words of the song's title. I really like this arrangement, the way David builds around Ed Dillon's singing and then start to increase in intensity and dramatic effect. (9.125/10)A3. "And The Glory Of The Lord" (4:50) like a rock-orchestra arrangement of a gospel choir rendering of this liturgical song. The vocal arrangements are quite rich and sophisticated; the rock instrumentation a little out of place. (9/10)A4. "Behold" (2:35) led by a Black female Gospel-Blues singer (a Dillon?), acoustic guitar is the only support instrument for the first minute--the first verse. Slow development brings in blues-rock instrumentation with orchestral horn support. Carol Kaye's bass and the electric piano are the most prominent of the rock musicians. Nothing very special or even dramatic here. (8.75/10) B1. "Pastoral Symphony" (5:35) layers of strings open this one, presenting the melody in a kind of fugue before more sections of the orchestra are slowly brought in. This sounds a bit like a New Age "spreading out" of a Pachelbel song. Nice but, again, nothing ground-breaking or exceptional. (8.75/10) B2. "And The Angel Said Unto Them" (2:52) opening with the same orchestral strings, in the second half of the first minute the music eventually gives way to a R&B combo for a Black female soprano gospel singer to sing over. The full orchestra is quite present, serving as thick and integral support, though the drums, bass, electric piano, and electric guitar work are the most active and aggressive here--especially in the song's second half--as anything else on the album. (Could that have been Earl Palmer on the drums?) (9/10) B3. "Glory To God" (3:03) elements of both female and male choirs are presented as opposed, woven, and antiphonal/echoing parts of the lyrical presentation while gentle funk-rock band and full symphonic orchestra participate from start to near-the finish. Quite a disciplined performance that David got out of these singers (as well as the orchestra). (9.125/10)B4. "Hallelujah" (3:23) we all know and love it. This one sounds like a slightly slowed-down, BARRY WHITE-version of the tune--until, that is, the second minute when the music moves into an all-instrumental section where Don, Mike, and the orchestra's horn section are given a little room to express themselves in solos. But then we return to the horn-embellished vocal delivery. I have to admit that I've heard many versions of this "song" that I like far better. (8.75/10)B5. "Worthy Is The Lamb" (2:52) nice Gospel choir music with totally-unnecessary and unfulfilling rock instrumentation. Even the orchestral work on this one feels as if it "gets in the way" of the fine vocal work. "The Dillons" are definitely a fine choir. (8.875/10)Total time: 32:40I have to say that this was one of the few times that I actually thought that the great Carol Kaye's bass playing was unbefitting to the music, which feels really weird since I revere her work and instincts so highly. Where I think David's work--his "Rock Interpretation"--started really strongly, I think it went off the rails somewhere in the middle of the Second Side. B+/4.5 stars; a near-masterpiece of the fusion of rock, jazz, R&B, and classical musical styles.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是David Axelrod在1971年对亨德尔《弥赛亚》的摇滚化改编，以38人交响乐团搭配摇滚节奏组，在洛杉矶录制完成。制作人Julian "Cannonball" Adderley，演唱由团体The Dillons承担。整体编排从交响乐序曲出发，在中段加入哇音吉他、放克鼓组和电钢琴，形成古典编制与摇滚乐队的对峙与融合。各曲处理方式不同：有的以福音合唱为骨架配合管弦乐，有的以钢琴或原声吉他起底缓慢引入摇滚编制，也有纯弦乐层的展开。Carol Kaye的低音和Don Randi的键盘在摇滚段落中表现突出。整张专辑定位偏向当时流行的宗教摇滚潮流，编曲细致但在风格探索上较为保守，未走向更深的实验领域，跨类型融合虽存在但仍以亨德尔原作旋律为核心框架。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — D'Arcansiel, an Italian band with a French comically misspelled name (all the more strange given that the opening track of their 1988 debut album is aptly titled "Un Arc dans le Ciel"), which emerged in the mid-1980s and disbanded a few years later, we were familiar with their three neo-prog albums (including the quite respectable *Still Searching*, released in 1990), heavily influenced by Marillion from the same era, though none of them left a lasting impression on our minds, already saturated with prog masterpieces of all kinds. Suffice it to say, I wouldn't have bet much on a new Arcansiel album ? I would have been wrong, because that's exactly what just happened with *Hard Times*, an undeniable success in a very personal RPI style that easily makes you forget the band's earlier efforts. This proves once again, as the saying goes, that it's never too late to do things right. "Too Late!" Yet this is the painful cry of alarm delivered?through the voice of the excellent singer Marco Leccese and the band's new keyboardist Davide Sorella?right from the introduction of the first track, a nearly 18-minute suite that Sorella wrote and composed.The state of Planet Earth is cause for concern, and even if it's not certain that the point of no return has been reached, we can safely say that we will not leave this place in the same condition we found it. The beauty of the world is fragile, and humankind is a malevolent shadow that has never ceased to wither it away. Progress continues its rapid march regardless of the circumstances and seems to defy even the most alarming signs. So is it too late to avert disaster? Sorella tells us instead that it's too late to keep wasting our time making bad decisions or failing to take any serious action.Musically, "Too Late" is a grand symphonic prog epic as captivating and inexhaustible as the theme it explores. With a neo-Baroque-inspired leitmotif that gives center stage to a keyboard-dominated instrumental section (a commanding synth, a very assertive piano, a mischievous harpsichord, and a swift Hammond organ playing in rondo form), all in service of hyper-melodic vocal parts?reminiscent of what Oliviero Lacagnina has recently done with The Samurai of Prog, or even Gryphon at their most prog?this majestic epic manages to bathe discreetly in a fluid, slightly jazzy atmosphere, then bursts into a symphony that is more melancholic than desperate, at times bordering on the tragic. After such a fireworks display?18 minutes that seem to fly by in the blink of an eye and that one wishes could last an eternity?the rest might seem to take a back seat, less grandiose. But this impression quickly fades upon listening to the next three tracks, which are just as brilliant."Hard Times" (like the title of Dickens' novel), can be understood as "Difficult Times" but 'Hard' also means "Tough." We are indeed living in an era with problems that are difficult (but not impossible?) to solve on every level (social, cultural, ethical, ecological, political?); but we are also in a world that is hard to live in for many of us?and that "us" encompasses the majority of living beings. Arcansiel's album offers us some enlightening accounts of this. From the scathing and mocking "Puppets and Puppeteers" (a description of one of the most irritating aspects of new media) to the disillusioned "Heaven Is Not Here" (beware of smooth talkers and false promises), the social issues addressed in *Hard Times* are critical reflections that remain relevant and never fail to move the listener.The result of a collaboration between bassist Felice Lombardo and guitarist Sebastiano Valvo, "Puppets and Puppeteers " (7:51) brings a fairly distinct shift in musical atmosphere by adopting a deliberate tempo with irregular measures in a powerful neo-prog style reminiscent of early Asgard (Leccese's vocals play a part in this), illuminated by dazzling synth solos that readily give way to a magnificent lyrical guitar solo. "Heaven Is Not Here" (11:22), written by the bassist, also offers remarkable moments, especially for those who appreciate Jon Anderson's more peaceful work paired with Genesis's "Supper's Ready."Personally, I have a soft spot for the unpredictable "My Old Same Mistakes" (7:27), written by the duo Sorella and Valvo in a melodic style quite similar to the romantic, post-Gabriel era of Genesis, and in which Marco Leccese once again works wonders (his "Save Me," sung with great conviction, is sure to be memorable), though the second half?following a medieval-influenced instrumental bridge?leans toward a swaying jazz-rock style, before concluding with Canterbury-style prog, all seamlessly strung together. As surprising as it is delightful.More than 30 years have passed since *Still Searching*, and only drummer Gianni Lavagno remains to ensure the band's continuity and the legitimacy of the Arcansiel name, though he did not participate in writing the songs for *Hard Times*. The compositions penned by the other three musicians?evolving into a sort of shimmering neo-prog with a distinctly Italian sensibility, featuring numerous twists, breaks, and inspired resurgences?are far richer and more diverse than those of the original Arcansiel. Reusing the same name may seem like a questionable choice, even an abuse of the name. But after all, the label on the bottle isn't very important when it contains such nectar?to be savored without moderation to make our lives sweeter.
items._cn_summary: Arcansiel 是来自意大利的新前卫摇滚乐队，2024年发行专辑《Hard Times》。整张专辑以一首近18分钟的多乐章套曲开场，主题聚焦于地球生态危机与人类行动的迟缓。开篇曲目采用新巴洛克风格的固定乐思，由键盘主导，合成器、钢琴、大键琴与哈蒙德管风琴交替铺陈，配合旋律性极强的声乐段落，整体呈现出兼具史诗感与忧郁气质的交响化编曲。后三首作品延续了这一品质，虽规模稍小但同样扎实。该专辑延续了乐队早期对Marillion的借鉴脉络，但据乐评所述，其个人化意大利前卫摇滚风格已显著成熟。整张作品在结构编排与器乐融合上展现出较高的完成度，但整体仍属传统交响前卫范畴。

items.body: The Cult released their fifth studio album, “Ceremony,” on 23 September 1991, through Beggars Banquet in the United Kingdom and Sire in the United States. The English rock band, who had started the decade before as the post-punk groups Southern Death Cult and Death Cult, made the record as a two-piece with session players. It turns 35 this year. By the time the sessions began, the touring line-up had gone. Bassist Jamie Stewart retired and moved to Canada after the final leg of the “Sonic Temple” tour in April 1990, and drummer Matt Sorum left to join Guns N’ Roses, leaving vocalist Ian Astbury and guitarist Billy Duffy as the only official members. Todd Hoffman played bass and James Kottak drums on the demos. For the album itself, Mickey Curry returned on drums after his session work on “Sonic Temple,” with Charley Drayton on bass. Richie Zito produced, with Astbury and Duffy co-producing, and also contributed keyboards and harmonium. Benmont Tench played organ, piano and mellotron, Scott Thurston added synthesizer and piano to “If,” Suzie Katayama played cello on “Indian,” and Alex Acuña handled percussion on “Indian” and “Wonderland.” Tommy Funderburk sang backing vocals across most of the record, joined by Donny Gerrard, Mona Lisa and Yvonne St. James on “Sweet Salvation.” Phil Kaffel engineered, Mike Fraser mixed, and George Marino mastered the album at Sterling Sound in New York. Pre-production ran at Oliver Ferrand Studio in Los Angeles and Mates in North Hollywood, with recording at Music Grinder Studios in Hollywood and recording and mixing at A&M Recording Studios. The eleven tracks run 63 minutes and 38 seconds: “Ceremony,” “Wild Hearted Son,” “Earth Mofo,” “White,” “If,” “Full Tilt,” “Heart of Soul,” “Bangkok Rain,” “Indian,” “Sweet Salvation” and “Wonderland.” Astbury and Duffy wrote all of them. “Wild Hearted Son” opens with an excerpt from “The Grass Dance” performed by The American Indian Dance Theatre, and “White” quotes Lawrence Lipton’s 1959 book “The Holy Barbarians,” which Astbury took as the name of his next band in 1996. “Wild Hearted Son” was the first single, followed by “Heart of Soul” in 1992. “White” appeared as a single in Canada only, “Sweet Salvation” was issued in Argentina in 1992 as “Dulce Salvación,” and the title track came out as a promotional single in Spain. The cover photograph, taken by John Running, drew a lawsuit. The parents of the Native American boy pictured on the sleeve sued over the unauthorised use of their son’s image, a case Entertainment Weekly reported on 19 June 1992. The New York proceedings against Warner Bros. Records were dismissed in February 1997 for lack of personal jurisdiction; a separate action filed in the District Court of South Dakota on 10 April 1995 was terminated on 16 May 1995. The dispute held up the record’s release in several territories, with South Korea and Thailand not seeing it until 1992 and Turkey not until the band played Istanbul in June 1993. Alan Forbes handled the art direction and design with the band. “Ceremony” reached number 9 on the UK albums chart, was certified gold by the BPI, and went platinum in Canada. Sources differ on its US peak: Wikipedia’s entry on the album gives number 25 on the Billboard 200, while its entry on the band gives number 34. The Ceremonial Stomp tour took the record through Europe in 1991 and North America in 1992, with Michael Lee on drums, Kinley “Barney” Wolfe on bass and John Sinclair on keyboards. The album streams on Spotify. About The Cult Ian Astbury formed Southern Death Cult in Bradford, Yorkshire, in 1981, with guitarist Buzz Burrows, bassist Barry Jepson and drummer Aki Nawaz Qureshi. They played their first show at the Queen’s Hall in Bradford on 29 October 1981, signed to Situation Two, an offshoot of Beggars Banquet, and released the triple A-side single “Moya” in 1982 before ending after sixteen months with a final Manchester show in February 1983. Jepson went on to co-found Into A Circle with Paul “Bee” Hampshire in 1985. In April 1983 Astbury teamed up with Billy Duffy, who had played in the Nosebleeds alongside Morrissey, then Lonesome No More and Theatre of Hate. The new band, Death Cult, added bassist Jamie Stewart and drummer Raymond Taylor Smith, later known as Ray Mondo, both from the London post-punk group Ritual. Death Cult debuted live in Oslo on 25 July 1983 and released the “Death Cult” EP the same month, with the “Gods Zoo” single following in October. Nigel Preston, previously of Sex Gang Children, replaced Mondo that September. The group shortened its name to The Cult in January 1984, ahead of an appearance on the Channel 4 programme The Tube. “Dreamtime,” recorded at Rockfield Studios in Monmouth with producer John Brand, arrived in September 1984 and reached number 21 in the UK. Preston was dismissed in June 1985 and Big Country’s Mark Brzezicki played the “Love” sessions that July and August; the Steve Brown-produced album reached number 4. Les Warner drummed on the world tour that ran from late September 1985 to June 1986. The follow-up was first recorded as “Peace” with Brown at the Manor Studios in Oxfordshire, then re-cut in New York with Rick Rubin and issued in April 1987 as “Electric,” which also reached number 4. Kid Chaos joined on bass for that tour, with Stewart moving to rhythm guitar. “Sonic Temple,” produced by Bob Rock and recorded in Vancouver between October and December 1988, followed in April 1989 and went gold in the UK and platinum in the US. After “Ceremony,” Astbury and Duffy replaced the touring band in 1993 with Craig Adams of The Mission and drummer Scott Garrett, the line-up that recorded “The Cult” with Bob Rock in October 1994. The band split in March 1995 during a South American tour. Astbury formed Holy Barbarians, whose only album “Cream” came out in May 1996, and released the solo record “Spirit\Light\Speed” in June 2000. Duffy worked with Coloursound alongside Craig Adams and Mike Peters, then Dead Men Walking and Cardboard Vampyres. The Cult reformed in 1999 with Sorum and bassist Martyn LeNoble, signed to Atlantic for “Beyond Good and Evil” in 2001, and went on ice again in late 2002. Astbury spent that second break fronting the surviving members of The Doors in a group billed variously as The Doors of the 21st Century, D21c and Riders on the Storm. He announced his departure in February 2007, stating: “I have decided to move on and focus on my own music and legacy.” The Cult had already reunited in January 2006 with drummer John Tempesta, guitarist Mike Dimkich and bassist Chris Wyse. “Born into This,” produced by Martin “Youth” Glover of Killing Joke, came out on Roadrunner on 16 October 2007. Cooking Vinyl signed the band in May 2011 and released “Choice of Weapon” on 22 May 2012 and “Hidden City” on 5 February 2016, both produced by Rock. James Stevenson replaced Dimkich on rhythm guitar in 2013 and Grant Fitzpatrick replaced Wyse on bass in 2015. Duffy also appeared on Wayne Hussey’s 2020 charity remake of “Tower of Strength,” alongside members of Depeche Mode, The Smiths, The Mission, Gary Numan, etc.. The band signed to Black Hill Records in May 2020, began recording at Rockfield in August 2020 with producer Tom Dalgety, and released “Under the Midnight Sun” on 7 October 2022 with Charlie Jones on bass. On 23 October 2025 the group announced a touring hiatus of undetermined length to concentrate on writing and recording. “Ceremony,” the only album in that catalogue made without a settled line-up, turns 35 this year.
items._cn_summary: 本文是关于The Cult第五张录音室专辑《Ceremony》发行35周年的纪念性新闻报道，并非传统意义上的乐评。内容主要围绕专辑的制作背景、录音人员构成、曲目列表及发行信息展开：1991年发行时乐队仅剩主唱Ian Astbury和吉他手Billy Duffy两人为核心，邀集大量客座乐手参与录制，包括鼓手Mickey Curry、贝斯手Charley Drayton等。Producer Richie Zito主导制作，键盘与弦乐编配丰富。专辑收录11首曲目，时长约64分钟，封面因涉及原住民儿童肖像而引发法律诉讼。整体属于主流硬摇滚/另类摇滚范畴，与实验、前卫、电子或暗潮等先锋方向关联甚微，文章以信息整理为主，缺乏音乐性分析与深度评论。

items.album: Sandie Trash announces ‘Poupée Panik’, featuring Eric Debris and Richard Belgium
items.excerpt: Sandie Trash announces the single “Poupée Panik,” featuring Eric Debris (Métal Urbain) and Richard Belgium (MI6), the first track revealed from the upcoming album “Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka.” The French post-punk and new wave project has not confirmed a release date for the album itself, and “Poupée Panik” is not yet available on Sandie Trash’s Bandcamp page, Instagram or Facebook. Sandie Trash builds ‘Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka’
items.body: Sandie Trash announces the single “Poupée Panik,” featuring Eric Debris (Métal Urbain) and Richard Belgium (MI6), the first track revealed from the upcoming album “Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka.” The French post-punk and new wave project has not confirmed a release date for the album itself, and “Poupée Panik” is not yet available on Sandie Trash’s Bandcamp page, Instagram or Facebook. Sandie Trash builds ‘Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka’ around the Motel Dakota The nine-track album is set around a recurring fictional location, Room 17 of the Motel Dakota, with several tracks written as character pieces tied to that setting: “La perversita,” “Poupée Panik,” “Élégance déplacée,” “Gloria Dakota” and “Sophie qui aime les avions.” Sandie Trash describes the record as a “sabotage” of eighties nostalgia rather than a nostalgic homage to the decade. Alongside Eric Debris and Richard Belgium, the album credits a wide cast of guest contributors: Emmanuelle 5 (Dead Sexy), Olivier de Joie (Les Fils de Joie), Max Freeth (Ausgang), Karbokroma, Kelsey Warren (Blak Emoji), Jérôme Lefdup (Lefdup & Lefdup), Gilles Le Guen (Denner) and Oli Le Baron (Ici Paris). One track, “I Trash You Fuck Off,” is credited with a guest vocal from Helno, the former Lucrate Milk member who went on to front Les Négresses Vertes until his death in January 1993. Sandie Trash’s announcement does not explain how that vocal appears on a track dated 2026, whether as a sample, an archival recording or another arrangement, and no further detail was available to confirm it. Eric Debris also mixed and mastered the album at ATX Mastering studio. The cover art is by Italian illustrator Volt.B. About Sandie Trash Sandie Trash is a French punk and electro project based in Périgueux, fronted by the singer of the same name and built, album after album, around a rotating cast of guest musicians on individual tracks. The approach dates back at least to 2018, when the project’s “Le French Peep Show” paired a new musician with each song on the record. On Bandcamp, Sandie Trash’s confirmed discography includes the album “Outrageous brune,” released 25 February 2010 through Indies.Music.Productions with vocals from Sandie Trash and Maudd and mixing and mastering by Emmanuel Borie, and the 14-track compilation “Rose chewing-gun & Machine-gum (2006-2017),” released 29 May 2025 and gathering tracks and features from that decade, including contributions from Kloot Per W, Romeo Praly, Kim Ohio Fuzz, Marcel Vanthilt and Nina Courson. “Poupée Panik” and the album built around it, “Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka,” continue that same collaborative format on a larger scale, bringing in musicians tied to Métal Urbain, MI6, Ausgang, Denner and other underground post-punk and EBM circles for a post-punk and new wave record set inside the fictional Motel Dakota.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章是关于法国后朋克与新浪潮项目Sandie Trash新单曲及专辑发行的新闻通告。专辑以虚构地点Motel Dakota 17号房为核心，串联多首角色化曲目，邀请Métal Urbain、MI6、Les Négresses Vertes等地下后朋克与EBM圈子的音乐人参与合作。制作人将专辑定位为对八十年代怀旧情绪的'破坏'而非致敬，混音与母带由Eric Debris在ATX Mastering完成。值得注意的是，其中一首曲目使用了已故Helno的人声，具体来源未获说明。文章内容偏向新闻稿性质，缺乏对音乐实际声响与艺术表现的分析，信息量虽较充实但评论深度有限。作为来自法国的独立地下项目，文章所涉及的音乐风格与暗潮、EBM、后朋克等用户偏好领域有交集，但整体仍偏向传统新浪潮/后朋克路线，实验性元素有限。
